'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Insurgency in the North Caucasus]], [[Terrorism in Russia]]
**Six [[Police of Russia|law enforcement]] officers are wounded when a man they were trying to arrest blew himself up in the village of [[Uchkeken]], [[Karachay-Cherkessia]]. The [[Federal Security Service]] says no civilians were hurt and authorities were trying to establish his identity. [https://www.reuters.com/article/russia-attacks-blast/two-hurt-in-suspected-bomb-attack-in-russias-north-caucasus-ifax-idUSKBN28L14U?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Crime in Nigeria]]
**[[Kankara kidnapping]]
***Pupils are [[kidnap|kidnapped]] from a boys' boarding secondary school by an armed gang in [[Kankara]], [[Katsina State]], [[Nigeria]]. [https://bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-55288114 (BBC News)]   

'''Health and environment'''
*[[Climate change mitigation]]
**The [[European Council]] agrees to lower [[Greenhouse gas#Anthropogenic greenhouse gases|greenhouse gas emissions]] in the [[European Union]], compared to levels in 1990, by at least 55% before 2030. [https://apnews.com/article/europe-climate-climate-change-paris-summits-3c0ef69599fbf311353657f1ab6e672c (AP)]
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Northern Ireland]]
*****Restaurants, cafés, non-essential shops, and other venues that serve food, reopen in [[Northern Ireland]] after two weeks of [[COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns|lockdown]]. However, pubs that do not serve food will remain closed. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-northern-ireland-55251973 (BBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****[[Germany]] reports a record 29,875 new cases and 598 deaths in the past 24 hours, according to data from the [[Robert Koch Institute]], bringing the total number of confirmed cases to 1.27 million and the death toll to 20,970. [https://www.dw.com/en/coronavirus-germany-reports-record-cases-at-nearly-30000/a-55900582 (DW)]
****Due to an increasing number of new cases and deaths, [[Chancellor of Germany|Chancellor]] [[Angela Merkel]] and the leaders of 16 [[States of Germany|states]] are expected to discuss new restrictions at a meeting on December 13. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2020-12-11/german-virus-cases-and-deaths-rise-most-since-start-of-pandemic (Bloomberg)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Belarus]]
****[[Belarus]] reports 1,967 cases, a new single-day record. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2020-12/11/c_139582731.htm (Xinhua News Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal]]
****[[Portugal]] reports a record 95 new deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 5,373. [https://news.yahoo.com/portugals-daily-covid-19-deaths-180118730.html (Yahoo! News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports a record 613 new deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 48,593. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2020/12/11/russias-coronavirus-deaths-surpass-600-in-one-day-record-a72327 (''The Moscow Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Switzerland]]
****[[Switzerland]] orders restaurants, bars and shops in most parts of the country to close at 7pm, as the country faces a persistently high level of new cases and deaths. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-swiss/swiss-impose-7-p-m-shutdown-on-most-shops-restaurants-to-tackle-covid-19-idINKBN28L1NJ (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine]]
****[[Ukraine]] reports a record 285 new deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 14,755. [https://www.kyivpost.com/ukraine-politics/covid-19-in-ukraine-13514-new-cases-285-new-deaths-377125-active-cases.html (''Kyiv Post'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****[[Indonesia]] reports a record 175 new deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 18,511. [https://amp.kompas.com/nasional/read/2020/12/11/16430521/update-175-pasien-covid-19-meninggal-dunia-dalam-sehari-tertinggi-selama (''Kompas'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]] surpasses 80,000 total cases of [[COVID-19]]. [https://www.theedgemarkets.com/article/covid19-malaysia-logs-1810-new-cases-lifting-total-cases-80309 (The Edge Markets MY)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****The number of confirmed cases in [[South Korea]] increases by 689, the highest single-day increase reported in the country since late February, bringing the nationwide total to 40,786 cases. [https://m-en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20201211002700320?section=national/national (Yonhap News Agency)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in California]]
****[[California]] reports 35,468 new cases in the past 24 hours, a new single-day record since the [[pandemic]] began. It also reports a record number of hospitalized patients: 2,013, and record number of 2,669 intensive care patients. [https://abc7news.com/california-covid-update-ca-coronavirus-cases-stay-at-home-19-testing/8694559 (KABC-TV)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Nebraska]]
****[[Governor of Nebraska|Nebraska Governor]] [[Pete Ricketts]] announces that the [[Nebraska|state]] will lift their restrictions on indoor gatherings after hospitalizations in the state dropped to 20%. However, he also urges people to stay vigilant to prevent the spread of COVID-19. [https://omaha.com/news/state-and-regional/govt-and-politics/ricketts-says-covid-restrictions-may-be-relaxed-but-nebraskans-need-to-stay-vigilant/article_d8f4c0dc-3bd5-11eb-8701-4776c9bcf2df.html (''Omaha World-Herald'')] [https://www.ketv.com/article/nebraska-will-ease-some-covid-19-restrictions/34947720# (KETV)] 
***The U.S. reports 3,309 deaths from COVID-19, a new one-day record. [https://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-reaches-record-daily-toll-of-3-309-coronavirus-deaths-01607807599 (Market Watch)]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***[[Tozinameran]]
****The [[Food and Drug Administration]] announces that they have formally approved [[Tozinameran]], the COVID-19 [[vaccine]] developed by [[Pfizer]] and [[BioNTech]]. [https://www.cnbc.com/2020/12/11/pfizer-covid-vaccine-approved-fda-emergency-use.html (CNBC)]
****[[Mexico]] approves the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine]]. [https://apnews.com/article/bahrain-coronavirus-pandemic-mexico-city-mexico-1e460dc0aae578435235a93569d739fa (AP)]
***[[Egypt]] receives its first shipment of 50,000 of [[Sinopharm]]'s vaccine, making it the first African country to receive COVID-19 vaccines. The shipment was provided as a gift from the [[United Arab Emirates]], which recently announced that the vaccine had an 86% efficacy based on [[Phase III clinical trials|Phase III]] testing results. [https://egyptianstreets.com/2020/12/11/egypt-receives-first-50000-batch-of-chinese-covid-19-vaccine/ (Egyptian Streets)]
***[[Australia]] stops a [[clinical trial]] of a COVID-19 vaccine candidate made by [[CSL Limited]] and the [[University of Queensland]] after trial participants returned false positive [[HIV]] results. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2020-12-11/uq-csl-coronavirus-vaccine-trial-to-be-abandoned/12973656 (ABC Australia)]
***[[Sanofi]] and [[GlaxoSmithKline]] announce that their COVID-19 vaccine candidate will not be ready until the end of 2021. [https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20201211-sanofi-gsk-announce-delay-in-covid-19-vaccine-until-end-of-2021 (France 24)]
***The [[First presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]] announces that they will purchase an additional 100 million doses of [[Moderna]]'s [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/amp/news/trump-administration-to-buy-additional-100-million-doses-of-moderna-vaccine/ (CBS News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Namibia]]
***[[Namibia]] reports a new single-day record of 324 cases, bringing the total number of confirmed cases since the start of the pandemic to 16,097. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2020-12/11/c_139582649.htm (Xinhua)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
***[[New Zealand]] creates its first "travel bubble" with the [[Cook Islands]], citing low COVID-19 infection rates and their "special ties". The travel bubble will allow citizens to travel between both countries without having to [[quarantine]] in early 2021. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-health-coronavirus-newzealand/new-zealand-creates-its-first-travel-bubble-with-cook-islands-idUKKBN28M00R?il=0 (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Pennsylvania]]
**[[John E. Jones III]], a [[United States federal judge|federal judge]] for the [[United States District Court for the Middle District of Pennsylvania|Middle District of Pennsylvania]], announces that he has rejected a bid to temporarily block [[List of governors of Pennsylvania|Governor]] [[Tom Wolf]]'s statewide mask mandate and contact tracking system. [https://www.pennlive.com/news/2020/12/we-are-all-fatigued-us-judge-rejects-bid-to-void-pas-mask-mandate-covid-19-contact-tracking-system.html?outputType=amp (''The Patriot-News'')]  
*[[2020 Hong Kong national security law|Hong Kong national security law]]
**[[Pro-democracy camp (Hong Kong)|Pro-democracy]] tycoon [[Jimmy Lai]] is charged under the new [[national security]] law. Lai faces a lengthy prison sentence for allegedly "conspiring with foreign forces" to endanger national security. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-china-55271020 (BBC News)] 
*[[Assassination of Rafic Hariri]]
**The United Nations-backed [[Special Tribunal for Lebanon]] sentences a [[Hezbollah]] operative to five concurrent [[life in prison|life]] terms ''[[Trial in absentia|in absentia]]'' for his role in the 2005 [[assassination]] of [[Rafic Hariri]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/12/11/hezbollah-operative-sentenced-to-life-over-hariri-killing (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Kyoto Animation arson attack]]
**Shinji Aoba, who is accused of killing 36 people by setting them on fire in last year's attack, is to be indicted on charges of [[murder]] after being found mentally competent to stand trial following a [[mental health]] evaluation. [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2020/12/11/national/kyoto-animation-arson-attack/ (''The Japan Times'')]
*[[Islam in Austria]]
**[[Austria]]'s [[Constitutional Court (Austria)|Constitutional Court]] overturns a [[government of Austria|government]] ban on school children wearing specific religious head coverings, ruling it discriminatory, and saying that the ban could lead to the "marginalisation of Muslim girls". [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-55277840 (BBC News)]
*After 51 years, a team of volunteer [[Cryptanalysis|codebreakers]] solved a [[cipher]] by the infamous [[Zodiac Killer]], according to the [[Federal Bureau of Investigation]]. The cipher says "I hope you are having lots of fun trying to catch me", and "I am not afraid of the [[gas chamber]] because it will send me to paradice {{sic}} all the sooner because I now have enough slaves to work for me". [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-crime-zodiac-killer/volunteer-sleuths-crack-zodiac-serial-killers-coded-message-idUKKBN28L2YC?il=0 (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Post-election lawsuits related to the 2020 U.S. presidential election]]
**The [[Supreme Court of the United States|United States Supreme Court]] denies ''[[Texas v. Pennsylvania]]'', a lawsuit filed by [[Texas Attorney General]] [[Ken Paxton]] to [[Attempts to overturn the 2020 United States presidential election|invalidate]] [[President-elect of the United States|President-elect]] [[Joe Biden]]'s victories in [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]], [[Michigan]], [[Wisconsin]], and [[Pennsylvania]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-55283024 (BBC News)]
*[[2020 Armenian protests]]
**Anti-[[government of Armenia|government]] protesters block streets in the [[Armenia]]n capital [[Yerevan]], continuing calls for [[Prime Minister of Armenia|Prime Minister]] [[Nikol Pashinyan]] to resign over the [[Nagorno-Karabakh]] [[2020 Nagorno-Karabakh ceasefire agreement|ceasefire agreement]] with [[Azerbaijan]]. [[Riot police]] detain more than 40 protesters. [https://www.rferl.org/a/armenia-pashinian-protests-resignation-elections-nagorno-karabakh/30995780.html (RFERL)]
*The [[United States Senate]] approves the $740 billion [[National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021]] (NDAA) by 84 votes to 13, which would be sufficient to override a possible [[Veto#Federal government|presidential veto]]. [[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]] objects to [[Section 230]] of the [[Communications Decency Act]] that currently provides [[legal immunity]] to [[social media]] companies, and also to a provision in the NDAA that will prohibit [[military base]]s to be named for [[Confederate States of America|Confederate]] generals. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-defense-congress/u-s-senate-backs-massive-defense-bill-defying-trump-veto-threat-idUSKBN28L24P (Reuters)]
